role: President, Federated Conservationists of Westchester County, Inc.
stance_basis: letter explicitly calls for closing all Interior lands to ORV use on energy and environmental grounds
summary: Mrs. David C. Donaldson, as President of the Federated Conservationists of Westchester County, Inc. (FCWC), submitted a letter arguing that the Draft EIS failed to adequately address the growing energy crisis and that encouraging ORV recreational use on public lands would exacerbate demand on shrinking petroleum supplies. She urged adoption of the alternative to close all Interior lands to ORV use, except for emergencies, framing it as both an energy policy and environmental responsibility issue.
complaint_summary: FCWC argues that the Draft EIS insufficiently addresses the energy crisis and that opening public lands to snowmobiles and ORVs increases demand on scarce petroleum supplies, recommending closure of all Interior lands to ORV use except for emergencies.

statement.text:
These comments are submitted in response to the Draft Environmental Impact Statement of the Department of the Interior, dated May 27, 1972, published June 2, 1972, with regard to Departmental Implementation of Executive Order 11644 Pertaining to Use of Off-Road Vehicles on the Public Lands.
Apart from the normal environmental considerations, not enough attention has been paid in the draft statement to the growing energy crisis, as it has been termed, and the effect upon the domestic economy and transit generally of increasing reliance on imports to meet our growing fuel and energy needs.
In light of this, FCWC questions, as a matter of national policy, the encouragement of recreational use, through the opening of public lands to snowmobiles and off-road vehicles, with the consequent increasing demand upon ever-shrinking petroleum and energy supplies.
This would indicate, on the basis of national policy, the wisdom of adoption of the alternative as referred to in Item "4" of the Draft Statement, to close all Interior lands to ORV use (except for emergency purposes, of course). Eventually, we may simply find that priorities in use of scarce petroleum resources require further limitations on use thereof by recreational vehicles.
The Department of the Interior, as a matter of environmental responsibility, must take this into consideration in establishing its current land use policy on land administered by the Department.
Sincerely,
600
Mrs. David C. Lonaldson
anne Donaldson
Fresident
